title: Foundational Skills
before:
Play-based and project-based pedagogies are common interdisciplinary models in early childhood education. However, best practice often requires direct instruction of knowledge and skills. On the surface, these two ideas seem to contradict — in reality, they are powerful practices when combined. These modules on interdisciplinary instruction specifically address the unique needs of students developing foundational literacy and math knowledge and skills.

Foundational Skills & Interdisciplinary Instruction

Introduction
  • Early Learning Foundational Skills - This page from the Early Learning Team focuses on strategies for building foundational skills in early elementary school.
  • Play-based Programming (PK–2) - This resource from the Early Learning Team explores "For Me" Instructional Programming.
  • Kids Can Learn More From Guided Play Than From Direct Instruction - This article discusses research findings on the impact of guided play.
  • Innovative Practice: 5 Strategies for the Early Learning Classroom - This article offers ideas for incorporating play- and project-based learning.

Literacy & Math Foundations

Literacy Foundations
  • Early Learning Foundational Skills: Literacy - This page from the Early Learning Team provides resources to build foundational literacy skills.
  • 5 Research-Backed Ways to Build Better Readers - This article shares 5 ideas to build stronger student readers.
  • Developing Strong Foundational Skills in Children - This article looks at the roles that the community, families, schools, and district leaders play in building strong literacy skills.
Math Foundations
  • Early Learning Foundational Skills: Mathematics - This page from the Early Learning Team provides resources to build foundational math skills.
  • 5 Ways to Build Math into Your Child's Day - This article shared 5 ways that anyone can incorporate math into a student's regular day.
  • Building Strong Foundations for Early Math Skills - This article offers ideas and resources to build strong math foundations at home and in the classroom.

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 1 heading sits at a level the page never opens — "" is an h6 with no h5 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 3 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — kathy.bertini@maine.gov → Kathy.Bertini@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 9 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 10 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Set a job title the way the rest of the site does
decisions.why: 1 job title sits in plain text under the person's name, where 186 elsewhere on the site are in italics — so the same contact block is drawn two ways depending on the page, and the title runs into the name above it. The standard here is the site's own, not a preference: two thirds of these blocks already do it. No word changes.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 1 description begins with a small letter, because it used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
